# Phases 8–12 — the wiring pass

**35 modules · 61 routes pending.** Generated by
`womencrafts-frontend/frontend/checks/fullstack-survey.mjs` — re-run it rather
than quoting this file. Phases 1–7 are done (7 was Money: 6 modules, 10 routes,
every button pressed against the real server).

## Why these phases and not others

The order is by **what it costs a woman when the screen is wrong**, not by how
much code each takes. A screen that says "Paid" without paying costs her money
and a fortnight of chasing it. A screen showing a hardcoded list costs her a
wasted trip. Both are bugs; they are not the same bug.

The pattern is known: `/checkout/[orderId]` held two hardcoded orders and a Pay
button that waited 1.1 seconds before announcing "Paid" without ever calling
the API. It rendered perfectly and passed every check it had. Nearly every
screen below is a variant of that, and for almost all of them **the backend
already exists** — this is wiring, not building.

## Done means, for every phase

Carried from `module-money.md`, because it is what made Phase 7 hold:

1. Every button either navigates, calls the API, or is deliberately inert and
   says so in a comment.
2. A check that **presses each one and asks the server** whether it heard —
   not that the screen changed. Screens change on their own.
3. The check seeds what it consumes, so it can be re-run.
4. Reads go through `useResource`, writes through `useAction`; money in minor
   units; independent queries in one `asyncio.gather`.
5. Both themes, no contrast or hit-target failures.
6. `bench.py --compare` — query count has not risen.

---

## Phase 8 — Screens that lie about money and records — **DONE 2026-08-26**
**2 modules · 9 routes.** Proven by `ux-circles`, `ux-circles-pay`, `ux-vault`
and `ux-business` — 40 assertions, every one asking the server what it thinks
happened.

### What it turned out to be

The plan said "wiring, not building" for Circles. That was wrong: the backend
had **no savings-circle concept at all**. Its circle was a discussion circle —
topic, posts, join, leave — while every screen in the module modelled a bachat
gat with a monthly share, a pot and a turn order. So Phase 8 built that:

- `is_savings` and `monthly_minor` on the circle, and `turn` on the member.
  Whether a circle collects money was previously decided by **a regex on its
  name**, which gave a Pay button to "Savings tips" and withheld one from a
  bachat gat called "Ladies Group".
- `circle_contributions`, with a unique index on `(circle_id, user_id, round)`.
  Paying twice for one round is now impossible by construction rather than by
  a check that two simultaneous taps would both pass.
- `GET /circles/{id}/savings`, `POST /circles/{id}/contribute`,
  `POST /circles` and `POST /shop/orders/{id}/cancel`.
- The round is **derived from the start date**, so no scheduled job has to tick
  circles forward and one nobody opened for three months is in the right round.

### What was actually broken

| Screen | What it did |
|---|---|
| `/circles/[id]/pay` | read **"Pay ₹0"** — the amount was never mapped — above eleven invented women, and a timer said "paid" without sending anything |
| `/circles/[id]` | printed **"Sunita Devi takes the pot"** on every savings circle in the app, whoever was next; join/leave only ever set a local flag, and `useState(c?.joined)` ran before the circle arrived so a member was invited to join a circle she was already in |
| `/circles/new` | "Create the circle" set a flag; the screen announced "&lt;name&gt; exists" about a circle that did not |
| `/documents/vault` | four upload buttons, all timers; a file size picked from a list of three by row position; and a **"Used by: Mudra Yojana"** list beside its own warning that removing a paper "can quietly stop a loan application" |
| `/documents/service/[id]`, `/documents/product/[id]` | both said "Saved." without saving — and both opened **completely blank** on a listing that had a name and a price, because `useState(() => …)` ran before the fetch returned |
| `/documents`, `/documents/order/[id]` | moving an order along and cancelling it were local state only — the buyer's order never changed |

### Two things worth keeping

`ApiDocument` described the *identity-check* document, not `/me/documents` —
`original_name`, `submitted`, `reviewed_at`, none of which that endpoint
returns. Every field read `undefined`, and the screen filled the gap with a
hardcoded list. The same class as the wallet mapping in Phase 7.

The vault was wired to `POST /verification/documents`, which puts an account
into review and **refuses outright once she is verified** — so it could never
have accepted a paper from anyone who had finished signing up. Adding a paper
now goes to `POST /me/documents` and leaves her verification alone.

| Module | Routes | What is wrong |
|---|---:|---|
| **Circles** | 4 | `/circles/[id]/pay` **fakes a savings-circle contribution** — a timer flips it to "paid" and nothing moves. `/circles/[id]` and `/circles/new` read nothing. Server exists: `/community/circles`. |
| **Your business** | 5 | `/documents/vault` fakes upload, download **and delete** — a woman can believe her Aadhaar copy is stored, or gone, when neither happened. Server exists: `/me/documents`. |

Delete faked as success is the one to be most careful with: it is the only
button here whose lie cannot be undone by pressing it again.

## Phase 9 — Screens that silently drop what she sends — **DONE 2026-08-26**
**3 modules · 5 routes.** Proven by `ux-work` — 14 assertions.

This one really was wiring: every endpoint existed. What made it slower than
that sounds is that two of the three were broken in a second way underneath.

- **`apiRequestMentor` sent `{ note }`** — a field the endpoint does not have,
  while `goal` is required. Wiring the button alone would have produced a
  validation error, and the right one: a mentor reading "someone wants to talk"
  with no subject cannot prepare or decide to say yes. The screen had no field
  for it either, so one was added.
- **The opportunities list was worse than faked.** Its filter memo left `JOBS`
  out of the dependency list, so the filtered set was computed once from the
  mock fallback and never again — the screen showed **invented listings for the
  whole session**. Same shape as the mentors memo that showed 6 of 24.
- **`applied` and `saved` were carried by the API and never read.** A woman who
  applied last week opened the screen to "Apply now" with no sign she had, and
  the Saved tab was empty on every visit whatever she had bookmarked.

An older `.bak` of the mentor screen already had the correct call. It had been
replaced by the faked version at some point.

| Module | Routes | What is wrong |
|---|---:|---|
| **Find work** | 2 | `/opportunities/[id]` — the job application is never sent. She waits for a reply to something nobody received. Server exists: `/growth/opportunities`, `/growth/applications`. |
| **Mentors** | 2 | `/mentors/[id]` — the request to a mentor is never sent. |
| **Feedback** | 1 | `/feedback` — never sent. Server exists: `/feedback`. |

## Phase 10 — Her own record, invented — **DONE 2026-08-26**
**4 modules · 13 routes.** Proven by `ux-account-settings` — 18 assertions.

These screens did not merely fail to save. Most of them showed **a life that
was not hers**, in specifics she could check against her own memory:

| Screen | What it told her |
|---|---|
| `/progress` | she had earned **₹1,48,500**, delivered 87 orders, and brought in three women — **Meera, Sunita and Farah**, by name. She had earned ₹9,497 and referred nobody. It also said "fourteen months since you joined" to a woman who joined this month. |
| `/settings/account` | a phone number, **"Jaipur, Rajasthan"**, a date of birth and "I sew, and I am learning to sell online" — as her own details. She lives in Mumbai. |
| `/settings/security` | **"An unknown phone · Safari on iPhone · Delhi · 3 weeks ago"**, listed as a device signed into her account |
| `/schedule` | five entries in May, including a mentor session with somebody called Neha and a mela at "Community Hall, Sector 12" |

The security one is the worst thing found in this whole pass. That screen is
what a woman opens when she is afraid somebody else is in her account, and some
of the women this is for have a real reason to fear exactly that. It told every
one of them that a stranger in Delhi had been there.

### What was built

- **`useJourney`** — her journey assembled from five concurrent reads
  (progress, wallet insights, shop summary, referrals, circles). Milestones are
  derived from events that actually happened, and each says "Not yet" rather
  than claiming a date.
- **`useDiary`** — deliberately **not** its own collection. A diary with its own
  store would drift from Bookings the first time somebody cancelled on one
  screen and not the other, and then two screens would disagree about where she
  is meant to be on Thursday. It reads bookings, registered events and accepted
  mentor sessions, and merges them.
- **`useDevicePref`** — a `useSyncExternalStore` hook for the settings that
  genuinely belong to a device rather than an account (bigger text, wifi-only
  downloads, the wake word). Reading storage in an effect cascades a render;
  reading it during render breaks hydration; this is the API for that shape.
- **Notification preferences grew from five fields to nine.** The screen had
  eight switches against five server fields — money, orders and circles had
  nowhere to go, so a wired Save would have discarded them silently.
- **`bio` on the member profile**, so the "line about you" has somewhere to live.
- Language now persists to her account, not just this browser. The user model
  already said locale "follows them across devices"; nothing wrote it.

### Sessions: a gap, stated rather than filled

There is no per-member session tracking — the `sessions` collection has no
`user_id`, and the `/sessions` endpoints are staff-gated. Building it properly
means recording and revoking tokens in the auth layer, which deserves its own
pass rather than a rushed add-on inside a UI phase; a half-built session list is
worse than none. So the screen now says plainly that we do not keep that list,
and points at the one thing that genuinely ends other sessions — changing the
password, which is now wired.

### One mistake worth recording

The first version of this phase's check found the "A line about you" field by
walking the DOM for its label text and guessing at a parent. It matched the
wrong element and typed its test sentence into her **name** and her **date of
birth**, on the live seed, twice. Both were restored. A check that writes to a
profile has to be exact about which box it types in, and put back what it
changed — it now does both.

| Module | Routes | What is wrong |
|---|---:|---|
| **Settings** | 9 | five routes read nothing — language, notifications, offline, security, voice. `const SESSIONS =` is a literal: the "sign out other devices" list is invented. Server exists: `/me/settings`. |
| **Your journey** | 2 | `/progress` holds `const EARNED =`. Server exists: `/me/progress`. |
| **Verification** | 1 | `/verify` — 5 buttons, no writes; "Resend" resends nothing. |
| **Your diary** | 1 | `/schedule` holds `const DAYS =`. **No server** — the only `schedule` paths are backup and report schedulers. Needs building. |

## Phase 11 — Content screens on hardcoded data — **DONE 2026-08-26**
**5 modules · 7 routes.** Proven by `ux-safety` (12) and `ux-discover` (11).

### The panic button was not wired

`/safety` is the reason this phase mattered more than its place in the order
suggested. The alert button filled over a second and a half and then called
`setSent(true)`. **Nothing left the browser.** A woman in trouble held it, read
that her contacts had been given her location, and was on her own. The two
contacts it named — "Sunita Devi (Sister)" and "Meera Joshi (Circle member)" —
were a constant; hers are her sister and her mother.

Everything needed already existed: `POST /safety/alert`, `/safety/contacts`,
`/safety/helplines`, `/safety/alert/{id}/stand-down`. None of it was called.

Three further things came out of wiring it:

1. **The alert recorded that it had reached nobody.** `raise_alert` matched
   `{"notify_on_alert": True}` while `to_response` treats a *missing* field as
   yes — so contacts saved before that field existed were shown to her as "will
   be told" and counted zero. Now `{"$ne": False}`, so the read and the write
   agree.
2. **Nobody is actually messaged.** There is no SMS provider wired in, so
   `contacts_notified` is the number of people the alert *names for staff to
   reach*. The screen now says "Our team has it, with your sister and your
   mother named on it" — and tells her to call 112 as well rather than wait.
   Claiming a message was sent would have been the same lie in a new place.
3. Location is fetched, but **bounded at four seconds** and with high accuracy
   off. An alert that waits on a GPS fix is an alert that does not go out.

### The rest

| Screen | What it was |
|---|---|
| `/messages` | four invented conversations — a buyer, **Anjali Mehta**, asking for two inches at the back of a kurta nobody ordered. Typing a reply appended it to a local array. The server has one member conversation, hers with us; that is now what it shows, and it points at circles and mentor requests for the rest rather than pretending to contain them. |
| `/intake` | said above its button that "everything on your home screen is chosen from what you say here", and sent nothing. Its five needs used different keys from the server's own list, and its suggestions were hand-written cards — one a "Craft Mela — Jaipur, ₹300, twelve places left" that no office was holding. |
| `/help` | topic tiles advertising 8, 6, 7, 9, 5 and 6 answers — 41 against eight that exist. Counted now. |
| `/explore/*/[id]` | not broken at all: both are deliberate redirects to the real detail pages. A false positive my survey now recognises. |

### One old check was asserting the lie

`ux-account.mjs` tested that holding the alert button made the page say "have
been told where you are". That sentence *was* the bug. It now asks the server
whether an alert exists, and stands it down afterwards.

| Module | Routes | What is wrong |
|---|---:|---|
| **Explore** | 3 | `/explore/program/[id]` and `/explore/service/[id]` — course and service detail pages read nothing. |
| **Messages** | 1 | reads nothing. `/me/messages` exists, but there are no member thread endpoints — part of this is backend. |
| **Help** | 1 | `const TOPICS =`. |
| **Safety** | 1 | `const CONTACTS =` — **check this one against the route-safety rule**: an invented emergency contact is the fabrication in this app that could get somebody hurt. Server exists: `/safety`. |
| **What you need** | 1 | `/intake` — the onboarding questionnaire writes nothing. |

## Phase 12 — The five the survey found late — **DONE 2026-08-26**
**4 modules · 5 routes.** Proven by `ux-learning` — 9 assertions. Every route
in the app now reads the server and fakes nothing: **0 remaining.**

Two things came out of it that were not just wiring:

- **`progress` and `sessions_attended` were two records of one fact, and
  nothing made them agree.** A lesson marked finished moved the percentage;
  the curriculum's `done` flags were built from the session count, which had
  not moved. So the course showed 20% complete with every lesson unfinished,
  and she came back to a course that had forgotten her. `_reached()` now takes
  whichever is further along, so neither can silently undo the other.
- **Two more stale memos**, on `/programs`: `TOP_PICKS` was missing from both
  dependency lists, so the course list and its category chips were computed
  once from the mock fallback and never again. The same shape as the
  opportunities list in Phase 9 and the mentors list before it. That is four
  screens with this bug; it is worth a lint rule rather than another fix.

These are not in the original plan. They surfaced
after it was written, when the survey learned to catch the quieter half of the
lie — `onClick={() => setSaved(true)}` with no timer attached.

Every one of them has its endpoint already. This is wiring.

| Route | What it fakes | What backs it |
|---|---|---|
| `/programs/[id]/lesson/[n]` | marking a lesson finished, and finishing the course | `PATCH /me/programs/{id}/progress` |
| `/programs/[id]` | saving a course | `POST /me/programs/{id}/enroll`, `/leave` |
| `/digital` | ticking off a step of the phone course | `GET /digital`, `POST,DELETE /digital/{step_id}/done` |
| `/health` | ticking off a health check-up | `GET /wellbeing/health`, `POST /reference/{id}/mark` |
| `/group-buy` | joining a group buy | `POST,DELETE /group-buy/{id}/join` |

`/programs/[id]/lesson/[n]` is the one to do first. A woman working through a
course marks a lesson done, closes the app, and comes back to find she has not
started — and the certificate at the end depends on the same count.

## Carried over, after the phases

From `RESUME-HERE.md`, unchanged:

1. `growth.opportunities` stores pay as **free text** — cannot be filtered or
   sorted, breaks the minor-units rule. Migrate to `pay_low_minor` / `pay_high_minor`.
2. Rename backend `/wallet/support` → `/wallet/fee-help` (collides with the
   `/app/support-fund` screen).
3. Five fields the API does not carry, each shown as "not known" rather than
   invented: route safety after dark, a mentor's fee, a circle's turn order,
   per-listing sales, reply times.
4. Redis for the cache and the rate limiter before more than one worker runs.

Plus three left open from Phase 7:

5. `ux-checkout` passes alone but fails in a back-to-back sweep — a flaky
   check, not a broken screen. Diagnose before trusting the suite.
6. `bench.py --compare` on the money endpoints.
7. Contrast and hit-target pass on the rebuilt checkout screen.
